## Finding

File-by-file review found that several historical Codex canary workflows remain manually runnable with `workflow_dispatch` and repository write / PR creation permissions.

This is not an immediate canonical-runner blocker because:

```text
- they are manual only
- they do not auto-merge
- they create PRs rather than merging
- they have changed-file guards for lab/index.html, lab/style.css, lab/app.js
- current weekly default-on path uses the canonical selected-prompt runner instead
```

However, some old canary workflows are intentionally weaker than the current canonical boundary, including old workspace-write or relaxed-sandbox experiments.

## Workflows reviewed in this group

```text
.github/workflows/codex-first-canary-run.yml
.github/workflows/codex-isolated-3file-canary-run.yml
.github/workflows/codex-isolated-3file-relaxed-canary-run.yml
.github/workflows/codex-writeback-canary-run.yml
.github/workflows/codex-offline-json-canary-run.yml
.github/workflows/codex-agent-observed-canary-run.yml
.github/workflows/codex-policy-agent-canary-run.yml
.github/workflows/codex-task-packet-canary-run.yml
.github/workflows/canary-007-policy-feasibility.yml
```

## Candidate release hardening options

Choose one before public release:

### Option A: Documentation-only

Keep workflows runnable, but clearly document that historical canary workflows are not the normal release path.

### Option B: Explicit repository variable gate

Require a repository variable such as:

```text
ALLOW_HISTORICAL_CANARY_WORKFLOWS=true
```

for older historical canary workflows to run.

This preserves the workflows as evidence surfaces while reducing accidental execution.

### Option C: Disable only weaker canaries

Gate only the old workspace-write / relaxed-sandbox canaries, while leaving read-only feasibility and canonical selected-prompt smoke workflows available.

## Non-goals

- Do not delete historical canary workflows in this issue.
- Do not remove run records or generated evidence.
- Do not change the canonical weekly selected-prompt default-on path.
- Do not enable auto-merge.

## Current recommendation

Use Option B or C if release hardening prioritizes accidental-run prevention.

Use Option A if preserving easy rerun access to historical experiments is more important.

issues.body:
## Purpose

PR #302 changed `Weekly Auto Run` so eligible weekly implementation candidates use the canonical Docker/Codex selected-prompt runner by default.

This issue now tracks the safer pre-release verification target first:

```text
ordinary default-on weekly run
→ support unlock resolved
→ vote summary PR created
→ no eligible candidates
→ no implementation-agent attempt
→ no Codex call
```

The eligible canonical implementation path remains a later release/operation verification target, not a pre-release requirement.

## Current status

```text
canonical weekly default: default-on
DEFAULT_USE_CANONICAL_SELECTED_PROMPT_RUNNER=true
legacy fallback: present and non-canonical
auto-merge: disabled
manual review: required
release state: not publicly launched yet
```

## Why no-eligible first

The workflow gates all implementation-agent and Codex steps behind:

```text
steps.eligibility.outputs.has_eligible == 'true'
```

If the no-change baseline wins or no prompt beats the baseline, the workflow should stop after the vote summary path and report:

```text
No eligible candidates. No implementation-agent attempt will be made.
```

This verifies default-on weekly operation without intentionally spending an implementation-agent run.

## Phase 1 verification checklist: no-eligible path

- [ ] `Support Unlock Export` completed for the target completed ISO week.
- [ ] `data/support-unlocks/<week-id>.json` exists and validates.
- [ ] `Weekly Auto Run` reads the support unlock file before vote collection.
- [ ] Vote summary PR is created.
- [ ] Vote summary PR records `Canonical selected-prompt runner: true` or equivalent default-on status in the weekly summary section.
- [ ] Selection metadata shows `baseline_won: true` or `eligible_count: 0`.
- [ ] The run logs contain `No eligible candidates. No implementation-agent attempt will be made.`
- [ ] No implementation PR is created.
- [ ] No Codex selected-prompt runner step executes.
- [ ] No implementation secret is required.
- [ ] Vote summary PR does not modify root lab implementation files.
- [ ] Auto-merge does not occur.
- [ ] Manual review remains required.

## Phase 2 verification checklist: eligible canonical path, later only

Run this only after release or when intentionally validating a real eligible prompt.

- [ ] Implementation PR body contains `Runner: codex-cli-selected-prompt-packet-container`.
- [ ] Implementation PR body contains `Canonical selected-prompt runner: true`.
- [ ] Changed files are only `lab/index.html`, `lab/style.css`, and/or `lab/app.js`.
- [ ] Safety check passed before PR creation.
- [ ] Static site check passed before PR creation.
- [ ] `weekly-selected-prompt-diagnostics-<run_number>` artifact exists.
- [ ] `weekly-selected-prompt-public-bundles-<run_number>` artifact exists.
- [ ] `weekly-selected-prompt-uploaded-bundle-verification-<run_number>` artifact exists.
- [ ] Public bundle verification passed.
- [ ] Uploaded bundle verification passed.
- [ ] Gitleaks finding count is 0.
- [ ] Auto-merge did not occur.
- [ ] Manual review remains required.

## Rollback signal

If default-on operation fails in a way that blocks ordinary weekly operation, set repository variable:

```text
PROMPT_VOTE_LAB_USE_CANONICAL_SELECTED_PROMPT_RUNNER=false
```

Then open a rollback PR that reverts `DEFAULT_USE_CANONICAL_SELECTED_PROMPT_RUNNER=true` and updates the status docs/tests.

## Non-goals

- Do not force an eligible prompt just to exercise Codex before public release.
- Do not remove `scripts/openai_lab_run.py` in this issue.
- Do not delete canary workflows in this issue.
- Do not enable auto-merge.
- Do not hand-edit generated snapshots.

## Summary

## Failure observed

`Codex Policy Agent Canary Run #10` failed in `verify_public_agent_run_bundle.py` with:

ERROR: Forbidden public pattern openai_key found in index.json

Gitleaks then scanned the same bundle and reported:

The custom OpenAI-key regex was too broad and matched `sk-` inside ordinary words such as `task-static...`.

sk-[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{12,}

(?<![A-Za-z0-9])sk-[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{12,}

Prompt Vote Lab participants need to see enough behavior evidence to improve future prompts:

- what files were visible
- which files changed
- which files were copied back
- what path model was used
- what sanitized stdout/stderr/install/mount logs showed
- what final action summary Codex gave

Publishing unsanitized logs is still unsafe, so this PR adds a publication sanitizer and observation index.

- Connect enrichment test to Script Check.

## Safety boundary

This does not publish raw private chain-of-thought.

It publishes sanitized stdout/stderr/install/mount diagnostics using best-effort redaction for:

- token-like strings
- environment assignment strings
- authorization bearer strings
- runner workspace paths
- temp paths
- GitHub workspace paths

If a real token is ever found in a public artifact, it must still be treated as an incident and rotated.

## Scope

Workflow, docs, scripts, and tests only.

## Summary

Automates support-unlocked comparison run eligibility using anonymized weekly support aggregates.

## Why

The support policy already defines these thresholds:

- 5 USD total weekly one-time support unlocks rank 2 comparison run
- 10 USD total weekly one-time support unlocks rank 3 comparison run

Before this change, weekly automation still depended on a manual `PROMPT_VOTE_LAB_SUPPORT_USD` variable. That is not fully automatic.

- No root `lab/` implementation changes.
